plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: Whole streets in eastern Australia turn lavender-blue as this tree opens its clouds of trumpet-shaped flowers. The blooms carpet the pavement below, so the color shows overhead and underfoot.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring in the Southern Hemisphere, peaking from October into November
plants.location: Brisbane and northern New South Wales, Australia, where flowering usually peaks first in late October
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America but has become a spring icon in cities from Australia to South Africa. Its fern-like leaves give it the species name mimosifolia, meaning mimosa-leaved.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: Cosmos is a cheerful annual with daisy-like blooms on airy, feathery stems. The flowers sway in the autumn breeze and keep attracting bees and butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer through autumn, roughly June to October, ending with the first hard frost
plants.location: Gardens across the temperate Northern Hemisphere, such as the US Midwest, in mild autumns
plants.funFact: Cosmos comes from Mexico. Its name comes from a Greek word for order or harmony, which refers to the neat symmetry of its petals.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy evergreen shrub blooms while most gardens are fading. Its delicate, often lightly fragrant flowers open in white and pink with golden centers of stamens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Autumn into early winter, usually starting in late September or early October
plants.location: Gardens in Japan, its native range, and in mild temperate regions such as the UK
plants.funFact: Sasanqua is a close relative of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis). Its seeds are pressed for camellia oil, which has long been used in Japan.
